title: Site evacuation procedure and offsite sanity checklist
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight operational run-through for performing a site 'evacuation' (planned or urgent) of a Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). It focuses on a short, deterministic sequence to get customer traffic away from a compromised/failed site, ensure offsite snapshots are consistent and verifiable, and promote a warm-standby in another region or private cluster. Intended for on-call SREs + private-deploy engineers; complements the formal DR playbooks (see linked artifacts).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies only to Private deployments managed with Terraform modules in our tf-modules repo and using S3/GCS-style offsite object storage for snapshots.
- Assumes state is stored remotely (remote backend + locking enabled).
- Assumes a warm-standby exists (either Dedicated or another Private cluster) with compatible model artifacts and runtime versions.
- Assumes KMS keys for snapshot encryption are available/rotated in the target region or have a recoverable key policy.
- Not covering full data rehydration for very large model stores (>10TB) — separate plan needed for those customers.

Primary goals (ranked):
1) Safety first: ensure no partial writes corrupt canonical artifacts.
2) Quick cutover: redirect traffic to standby to meet customer SLAs.
3) Verifiable integrity: cryptographic signature or checksums for offsite snapshots.
4) Repeatable rollback path: ability to return to original site once healthy.

Key contacts (on-call rotation):
- Primary DR lead: Priya Shah (me) - pager: @pri-shah, cake: vanilla
- Terraform modules owner: Ethan Park - slack: @ethan
- KMS/HSM ops: Lena Morales - slack: @lena-security
- Solutions eng for customer-specific cutover: Gita Raman - slack: @gita-se

Evacuation trigger scenarios (examples):
- Complete power/network loss to the rack or data center NOT recoverable within SLA window.
- Detected silent corruption of artifact store (checksum mismatch discovered during smoke).
- Sustained/severe performance regressions due to hardware failure that require full site drain.

Immediate triage (T+0 to T+15m):
- Confirm trigger and scope: which clusters, which tenants/customers?
- Post incident note in #private-deploy-dr channel and create a Linear DR ticket (tag: DR-urgent).
- Capture current terraform state version and last applied commit (tfstate object version + git sha).
- Verify remote backend lock state. If lock missing: escalate to modules owner.

Evacuation sequence (safe, ordered steps):
1) Freeze control-plane changes:
   - Disable CI pipelines that apply Terraform to the affected workspace(s).
   - Place a commit lock file in the deployment repo (DR-LOCK.txt) and update the ticket.
2) Graceful drain traffic:
   - Update smart-routing policy to remove site from preference (console route policy: prefer=standby-region).
   - For customer-critical routes, update DNS TTLs and issue a DNS swap plan.
3) Snapshot manifest and KV caches:
   - Trigger artifact store snapshot (cold snapshot + manifest export). Name: dr-<site>-<ts>.tar.gz and __manifest.json.
   - Export KV caches and any ephemeral routing state; store encrypted to offsite bucket.
   - Record checksums (sha256) and sign with DR signing key. Save signatures next to objects.
4) Verify snapshot integrity (parallel):
   - On a separate bastion or CI runner, download small manifest and verify checksums + signature using devops public key.
   - Run lightweight smoke validator (see smoke script path in linked artifacts).
5) Push to offsite storage and replicate:
   - Ensure replication completes to target region/replica bucket.
   - If replication fails, fall back to manual transfer (scp/gsutil) with chunked reupload plan.
6) Promote warm-standby:
   - Ensure terraform workspace in target region has matching provider versions.
   - Import snapshot manifest and run apply with minimal changes: scale up inference pools, attach storage.
   - Run model artifact checksum validation and cold-start acceptance tests.
7) Cutover traffic:
   - Move routing weights to standby (canary -> 50% -> 100% by 5–10 minute increments).
   - Monitor latency, error rates, and token-cost metrics closely for regressions.
8) Post-cutover monitoring window (4–24h):
   - Keep DR lead and module owners on call.
   - Do state hygiene: create a 'post-evac' snapshot of the promoted site.

Terraform module notes (quick compatibility checklist):
- Backend provider versions: ensure the aws/gcp provider versions match within one minor release across regions to avoid drift in resource semantics.
- State locking: always use state locking with DynamoDB/Cloud SQL for the backend. If the affected site’s lock service is down, coordinate with platform to temporarily allow manual lock override but log the event.
- Workspace/import strategy: for warm-standby promotion, prefer importing resources into an existing standby workspace versus creating a brand new workspace to preserve tfstate continuity.
- Module param mapping: keep a small compatibility shim that maps old module outputs to new module variable names during limited upgrades. Document shim in tf-modules/compatibility/README.
- Provider credentials: do not bake credentials into the artifacts. Use short-lived tokens and reference environment-based KMS key aliases for snapshot encryption.

Upgrade and rollback considerations during evacuation:
- If evacuation coincides with a planned runtime upgrade, prefer to pin the standby to the last known-good runtime/artifact version. Avoid mixing post-upgrade artifacts into the promoted cluster until stability window complete.
- Rollback path: keep the original tfstate and the last 3 snapshots (time-ordered) available. The rollback plan should be: re-import original state -> re-attach snapshot -> run smoke tests.

Validation and smoke tests (automated):
- Smoke checklist (automated runner):
   * infer_basic_prompt -> 200 tokens -> latency < 400ms p50 for target config
   * health-check endpoints return 200 and expected JSON schema
   * KV cache warmup sanity: repeated small prompts should have decreasing latency pattern
   * Auth and audit logs present and writable to target logging endpoint
- If any test fails, stop cutover and escalate. Document failure in ticket with logs and signatures.

Operational gotchas and notes to self:
- Signed manifests: were still onboarding customers for signature verification; for high-risk customers, request on-call compliance signoff before cutover.
- Snapshot size vs restore time tradeoff: prioritize smaller incremental snapshots for faster restore windows where the customer SLA demands it.
- KMS key cross-region access: pre-create key aliases in target region or have a documented key-wrap token flow.
- TF modules that assume local-only IPs need explicit CIDR remapping when promoted. Keep a mapping table in tf-modules/README.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- How to handle customer-specific dataset encryption keys that are only present in original site HSM? Current plan: require manual key escrow and a documented key-unwrap runbook.
- Should we automate manifest signing in the CI pipeline or keep it manual during DR? (Tradeoff: speed vs control)

Post-evac debrief and cleanup (T+24h to T+7d):
- Reconcile snapshots and remove stale offsite artifacts older than retention window.
- Rotate short-lived credentials used for transfer.
- Run a full integrity scan comparing pre- and post-evac manifests and log diffs.
- Update the tf-module compatibility matrix if any shim was applied. Open PR in tf-modules repo describing changes.

Checklist (quick) for on-call during evacuation:
- [ ] Create Linear DR ticket and post to #private-deploy-dr
- [ ] Freeze Terraform pipeline and add DR-LOCK
- [ ] Trigger artifact + kv snapshot and sign with DR key
- [ ] Verify signature & checksum on independent runner
- [ ] Replicate to offsite and confirm copy success
- [ ] Promote standby and import artifacts
- [ ] Run automated smoke tests and validate metrics
- [ ] Gradual traffic shift and monitor

References & links:
- tf-modules repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tf-modules (see compatibility folder)
- Smoke runner script: gh://redwood-inference/infra/ci/smoke/dr-smoke.sh
- Linear ticket: DR-341 (linked above)

TODOs (low priority):
- Add CI job to auto-sign manifests on snapshot completion (RFC in progress).
- Add a compact resume script that can wire up KMS aliases across regions.
- Create customer-facing post-evac runbook template for Solutions Eng.

Notes to future me:
- Keep this doc intentionally pragmatic. Most of the heavy-lifting (state migration, large restores) will be customer-specific and should be a separate SOW.
- If youre testing this, run it in the staging region with a simulated lock outage to validate manual override steps.

---
End of doc.
